metadata.title: Starting Strong Teaching and Learning International Survey 2018 Conceptual Framework (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a conceptual framework for the TALIS Starting Strong Survey 2018 rather than an empirical analysis paper. It describes the target populations (ECEC staff and centre leaders in ISCED Level 0.2, with an optional ISCED Level 0.1 under-3 component) and the thematic structure of indicators (staff-child interaction, monitoring/assessment, centre characteristics, leadership, climate, stakeholder relations, staff background, professional development, well-being, beliefs, self-efficacy, and equity/diversity). Because no analytic dataset, sampling frame, or estimation results are presented, the framework does not specify whether complex survey weights or replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are applied in estimation. For any subsequent empirical cycle using TALIS Starting Strong microdata, analysts should follow the survey’s sampling design documentation (Annex C in the framework) and apply the appropriate complex survey weights provided in the international database; however, this conceptual framework itself does not report weight variable names or weighting procedures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a conceptual framework document that does not estimate cognitive achievement outcomes using plausible values (PVs). The survey focuses on staff and centre leader self-report indicators and conceptual constructs (e.g., process quality, leadership, well-being, beliefs, self-efficacy, and equity/diversity) rather than reporting PV-based achievement scores in this document. Missing-data handling is therefore not described because no empirical model estimation or analytic sample is reported here.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined in this conceptual framework. The document specifies target populations (ECEC centres in ISCED Level 0.2, with an optional under-3 ISCED Level 0.1 component) and provides an overview of the survey’s conceptual model and indicator themes; detailed sampling and field-trial/main-survey design information is referenced as being available in Annex C, but no student-level inclusion/exclusion rules or analytic sample counts are reported in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD conceptual framework defines the theoretical and analytical underpinning for the TALIS Starting Strong Survey 2018, an international survey of ECEC staff and centre leaders in ISCED Level 0.2 (with an optional ISCED Level 0.1 under-3 component). It specifies the survey’s key themes and indicator domains, including staff-child interaction process quality, monitoring and assessment of children’s development/well-being/learning, centre structural and leadership characteristics, climate, stakeholder relations, staff and leader background, professional development, well-being, professional beliefs, self-efficacy, and equity/diversity in the child group. The framework emphasizes that the survey is cross-sectional and does not directly assess child outcomes, limiting causal claims about effectiveness. It also outlines policy relevance and interpretability principles (validity, reliability, comparability, and efficiency) and notes methodological considerations such as social desirability in self-report data and the use of situational judgment items to add perspective on process quality.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is intentionally sparse because the provided document is a conceptual framework and does not report an empirical ML/statistical analysis with an analytic sample, model training, PV handling, missing-data strategy, or performance metrics. As a result, fields such as total_students, countries with per-country Ns, and main_findings are not applicable to the framework text itself. The document does, however, specify the target populations and the indicator themes that would later be operationalized in the survey instruments and subsequent empirical analyses.
